clue.text: Demolish an impression with this kind of clue

parts.note: a pull is a printer's proof, an impression taken from type
this very clue is a Down clue, so the kind of clue is DOWN

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a clue built to knock down a solver's first idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This kind of clue' points at the clue itself: it sits in the Down list.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull down a building is to demolish it, a common phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Araucaria exemplifies this sort of diagram

definitions.text: Araucaria exemplifies this sort of diagram

parts.words: Araucaria exemplifies this sort of diagram
parts.note: Araucaria is the botanical genus of the monkey puzzle, a conifer, and also the pen name of a famous Guardian setter; a branching diagram shares the plant's name

explanation.surface: A remark that the famous setter Araucaria serves as a model for some kind of chart.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a celebrated Guardian setter, so the surface reads as about him; the genus of the monkey puzzle conifer gives the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey puzzle is a conifer, and a branching chart such as a family diagram is called by the same word.

clue.text: Cross words from one caught in traffic

indicators.note: something caught in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: traffic as a verb or noun means trade, dealing in goods
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Angry words from a driver stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' paints a road jam but means commerce; 'cross words' means angry words, not crossword entries.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is a stream of cross, that is angry, words.

clue.text: Theoretically practical 8, perhaps

definitions.note: in theory, as planned rather than as done in reality

parts.note: on means feasible or practicable, as in 'that plan is just not on'
8 across is GUARDIAN, an example of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Suggesting a newspaper might be practical in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across is GUARDIAN, the newspaper; 'practical' is ON, as in 'not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in theory rather than in practice, as plans look good before testing.

clue.text: Don from Oxford, say, with funny clue about time on run

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round another piece
funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RE means on, in the sense of concerning
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An Oxford don devising an amusing clue while short of time and on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a verb, to put on, but means a university teacher. 'about' puts the time letter inside the shuffled clue; 'on' is RE in the sense of concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A university don is a teacher, and one who gives talks to students holds that title.

clue.text: Kind of symmetry that's reasonable, incorporating old tradition, primarily

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: reasonable means sensible or logical, rational

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letters of the two words are used

explanation.surface: A claim that a form of symmetry is sensible because it draws on old tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes O and T from 'old tradition'; 'incorporating' puts them after the R of RATIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape unchanged by turning about a point has symmetry of the turning kind, one of the standard types.

clue.text: Boatman as main 22 down, say

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean
22 down is SETTER, a breed of gun dog, so it is an example of a dog

explanation.surface: Describing a boatman as the main crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief', but it is the sea; 22 down is the breed of gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sailor, a veteran mariner, is called by this salty phrase.

clue.text: Protector of child in a gun raid shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who shielded a child during an armed raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' fits the gun picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal custodian appointed to care for a minor holds this title.

clue.text: Grind away, getting the answer to crossword clue, finally

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Wearing oneself down while getting the solution to a clue at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like it modifies 'getting the answer', but it takes the last letters of 'the answer to crossword clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear something down gradually by friction is a synonym of grinding it away.

clue.text: Colluded, oddly, in something like this

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Self-referential: the word for the thing you are reading is tucked inside a word about conspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'strangely' but picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'Colluded'.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing being read is itself a crossword hint, so 'something like this' points to its own kind.

clue.text: A danger with a TV broadcast that's cutting-edge

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A risky TV broadcast that pushes the boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suits the TV picture but signals an anagram of A DANGER, A and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of the times and experimental, as at the leading edge of a field.

clue.text: No 1 piece of fiction in part of India

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a lie is an untruth, an invented story

explanation.surface: A top story set in a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' reads as 'best', but a football keeper traditionally wears shirt number 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The keeper in football or hockey traditionally wears the number 1 shirt.

clue.text: Finishing session on keyboard with nothing very loud after unusually long gig

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A keyboard player ending a session after an unexpectedly long, very loud gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' shuffles LONG GIG; O and FF come after. 'Keyboard' paints a musician but means a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a computer session by signing out is described by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Desires no end of money up front for what one's made

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: desires as a noun means longings, yearnings

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Desiring money at the outset for the money one has earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes Y, the end of 'money', and 'up front' places that Y at the front of the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Income or wages are the money a person has made from work.

clue.text: Crib clue from Crucible, for example

definitions.text: Crib clue from Crucible, for example

parts.words: Crib clue from Crucible, for example
parts.note: the letters of CRIB CLUE rearranged give CRUCIBLE, so one is a rearrangement of the other

explanation.surface: Looking for a cheat sheet clue in Arthur Miller's play The Crucible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crib' suggests a cheat sheet, but CRIB CLUE uses exactly the letters of CRUCIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging the letters of another is this kind of wordplay.

clue.text: Piece of verse a peasant composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A rustic writes a little poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suits verse writing but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two short syllables then a long one is a unit of verse.

clue.text: For me, goal is to tuck into health food

indicators.note: to tuck into means to put inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal, eaten as a health food
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone whose aim is to eat wholesome food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For me' is the setter speaking: this puzzle's setter is named in the byline. 'tuck into' reads as eating but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter refers to himself; the byline of this puzzle carries the setter's pen name.

clue.text: Business types putting a Conservative in the best of spirits?

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one letter goes inside another word

parts.note: genies are magical spirits, the most powerful kind in folk tales

explanation.surface: Firms putting a Tory in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the best of spirits' reads as 'very cheerful', but the spirits are genies. C goes inside GENIES after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies are businesses offering a service on behalf of clients, such as advertising firms.

clue.text: Left country without capital — new work either 22 could use

indicators.note: without capital means losing the initial letter, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Mexico is a country

explanation.surface: Someone left their country after the capital, then started new work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either 22' means 22 across or 22 down; both a puzzle compiler and a solver might use a word list. 'capital' is a capital letter, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary or word list is a reference work that crossword compilers and solvers both consult.

clue.text: Judge I'm entering final part of puzzle, say

indicators.note: final part of means the last letter of the following word
entering means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to say is to state

explanation.surface: A judge going into the last part of a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb STATE, which IM enters.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to estimate or gauge it.

clue.text: Small way in which soldier protects sleeping comrades?

parts.note: an entry is an entrance, a way in

explanation.surface: A small doorway through which a guard watches over sleeping troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a guard on watch protects comrades as they sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard posted on watch keeps comrades safe while they sleep.

clue.text: Second most important role in musical I rejected for you

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the title role is the lead in the musical Oliver!

explanation.surface: An actor turned down for the second lead role in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' is the setter addressing the reader, who is solving the puzzle. 'Second' is S, not 'second lead'.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter addresses the reader, who is the person working out the puzzle.

clue.text: Street being out of order, one provides direction to game

indicators.note: out of order means not in sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken street sign that once pointed the way to a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' reads as a sport but means hunted animals; a gun dog of this breed points them out.
explanation.definitionFit: This gun dog breed stands still and points towards hunted birds for the shooter.

clue.text: Estimating badly as puzzle expert

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Poor estimating by a supposed puzzle expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals an anagram of ESTIMATING.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker or solver of riddles and puzzles is called by this rarer word.

clue.text: A dozen players go after this role in Shakespearean comedy

definitions.text: A dozen players go after this
definitions.meaning: in ice hockey six players a side, twelve in all, chase the rubber disc
the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests actors, but it means ice hockey players, six on each team.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the disc chased in ice hockey and the name of the sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Saintly fellow — friendly type with top-class input

indicators.note: input means put in, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
U means upper class, in old British usage

explanation.surface: A holy man who is a friendly sort with upper-class contributions.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class is a British convention, from 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle to the Gentiles is a saint, so the name fits a saintly man.

clue.text: 8 22 down providing a lot of fun in endless career?

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside another
endless means without its last letter, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Asking whether a job without end gives plenty of enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: '8 22 down' means a Guardian setter: 8 across and 22 down. 'endless' and 'a lot of' each drop a final letter, and 'in' puts the trimmed fun inside the trimmed career.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving Guardian compiler uses this pen name, so he is a setter for that paper.

clue.text: Like our superior education, excessively on display?

parts.note: over means above, superior in position
us is the first-person plural, as in our

explanation.surface: Boasting of our superior schooling, shown off too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' looks like boasting but means placed over us.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used too often is excessively employed, as a cliche is.
